evidence.source: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks — 10,000-char cap is per hook output; overflow REPLACES the payload with a truncation preview (probe-verified on a live install, 2026-07-28)

Claude Code 2.1.259, probed on a live pane: `claude --permission-mode plan` renders `⏸ plan mode on (shift+tab to cycle)` beneath the input box. `modeLine` is the signature EVERY permission mode draws — the same line reads `bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)` under --dangerously-skip-permissions — so it locates the mode line; `marker` is what makes that line read-only. Locating and deciding are separate fields because a pane with subagents running draws `⏺ main` and one row per agent BELOW the mode line (live captures in test/medusa-wake.test.js, #783/#1101), so the mode line is not the last line and cannot be found by position.

busyMarker.source: First captured 2026-07-11 over four live sessions (#560 T2 spike). Re-measured on Claude Code 2.1.241 (#1114, throwaway session): `esc to interrupt` survives only inside a `low_priority_waiting` retry branch and is absent from an ordinary turn, so it is NOT sufficient on its own. Kept because that retry state is real and worth catching; the transcript-movement check carries an ordinary turn.

promptPattern.source: Live pane (#1109): an empty composer is the glyph plus a single NBSP, so the class accepts NBSP or one ordinary space and nothing else. The earlier `^\s*❯\s*$` accepted trailing whitespace, which let a half-typed space read as a bare prompt.

promptGlyph.source: Live pane (#1109): `❯` is the composer glyph, and the composer is located by it rather than by position — a pane with a running subagent fleet draws rows below the input box.

promptPad.source: Live pane (#1109): the separator the prompt itself draws between the glyph and the first input column is NBSP, with the cursor at column 2. Measured, not assumed — everything past exactly one separator cell is the operator's, a typed space included.

placeholderSgr.source: Live captures of both engines (#1105): Claude Code dims its inline suggestion with SGR 2 (faint), and genuinely typed input carries no styling at all. That second capture is what makes treating the attribute as 'not the operator's text' safe rather than reckless.

idleMarker.source: Measured and found ABSENT (#1114; #1106 left open). Across at rest, at rest with a faint suggestion, thinking, streaming and a backgrounded shell, no string is present at rest and absent mid-turn — the status and hint rows are byte-identical in both, and the bare prompt is drawn throughout. `null` records that measured gap, not an unattempted field.
